name: Register & Formality Analysis
description: Evaluates the sociolinguistic register of a text by measuring its adherence to formal, polite, and objective academic or professional standards. Commercial AI models (like ChatGPT or Claude) undergo rigorous Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) designed to make them 'helpful, harmless, and honest'. Consequently, their default output defaults to an unwaveringly polite, highly formal, and structurally rigid tone. Human writing, even in professional contexts, naturally exhibits 'register shifts'—momentary lapses into casual phrasing, expressive punctuation, or colloquial idioms. A text that maintains an artificially persistent, monolithic high-formality score is highly characteristic of machine generation.
mechanism: The analyzer utilizes a Part-of-Speech (POS) tagger and a specialized lexicon to scan for register markers. It penalizes the presence of contractions (e.g., 'don't', 'can't'), slang, idioms, expressive punctuation (e.g., '!!!'), and first/second-person pronouns which indicate an informal or conversational tone. It rewards complex prepositional phrases, passive voice structures, and objective, specialized vocabulary. The algorithm calculates the ratio of formal to informal markers and plots the variance of formality across paragraphs. A flat, consistently high formality trajectory with zero register variance strongly indicates the output of a safety-aligned LLM.
useCase: Particularly effective for analyzing blog posts, emails, social media content, and student essays, where natural human writing typically demands a conversational or mixed-register tone.
strengths:
• Highly effective against standard, out-of-the-box LLM generations which almost always default to a sanitized, formal tone.
• Computationally lightweight, relying on straightforward lexical matching and POS tagging sequences.
limitations:
• Easily spoofed if a user explicitly prompts the AI to 'write casually', 'use slang', or 'act like a teenager'.
• Generates false positives on highly formal human texts, such as legal contracts, peer-reviewed academic papers, or official corporate press releases.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical & Syntactic Register Scoring
Metric: Formal/Informal Marker Ratio & Register Variance
Output: 0-100 Formality Monolith Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-80% accuracy in casual domains. Less reliable in academic or legal contexts where human texts natively mimic AI formality. Best used in conjunction with perplexity metrics.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
